note: Issue #401: LAN play. One player hosts from F11 > Game, friends on the same wifi join by the host's address. Read by src/systems/net/net_session.gd. port: the UDP port the host listens on. max_players counts the host. send_rate: state packets a second each player sends. name_max: letters in a player's name. spawn_by_t89_m: how far from T-89 a guest stands on arrival. smooth_rate: how fast a remote body closes on where it was last heard (1/s); snap_m: further off than this it jumps. name_height: metres above the feet of the floating name; name_px its size on screen (the same at any distance). The other players on foot show on the F11 map as dots in mark_color; a click makes one the waypoint (a mark_color diamond on the HUD, the text white as any waypoint's), which clears within waypoint_arrive_m of them or when they leave. connect_timeout: seconds a join waits for the host before giving up. friendly_fire: your bolts and blade hurt the other players (each game applies the hits on its own player, times friendly_fire_scale); off, they pass through. It goes for ships too: while another player flies, your ship's cannons hit their ship (in the town's sky and out in space) and the hit lands on the ship they fly, in their game (shield, hull, shot down as by any gun); parked, their ship is a picture. Seekers never lock on another player's ship, but one flying straight (unlocked) that runs into it hits it. Your cannon shots and unlocked seekers in the town's sky show to the others. hitbox_radius / hitbox_height: the other players' bodies, for shots and for walking into. outfit_check_s: how often each game looks whether you changed what you wear, and tells the others. Issue #401 (guests' ships): each guest arrives next to a free landing pad (a town box of kind 'pad' with no ship on it and no remnant_ship, the host's game decides, spawn_by_pad_m past its edge) with a ship of their own on it (guest_ship) in one of the liveries (content/look/ships.json looks), by join order, labelled ship_tag over it (ship_tag_height metres up). Call flies it to them. Every player's ship (the one they fly, else their primary) shows in the others' games; one not heard of for ship_stale_s seconds goes. No free pad: by T-89, the ship on clear ground beside the pit. Issue #402 (one town): the host's game runs the town's people and sends them npc_rate times a second (those farther than npc_far_m from every player only every npc_far_every-th time), npc_chunk to a packet; a guest's copy walks to where the host's will be npc_lead_s from now and jumps there when more than npc_snap_m off, and npc_claim_s after the first snapshot a guest's own people that copy none of the host's go. peer_timeout_s: how long a player may not answer (a town loading) before the others count them gone. The host's time of day is everyone's on its planet: sent when it changes and every light_resend_s seconds; guests have no Time of day controls in F11. One space fight: the host's game runs the fight over its planet and sends its ships fight_rate times a second; a guest who climbs out while it is on flies copies of them (AI off), each closing on where the host's will be (from its speed, at most fight_lead_max_s ahead) at fight_smooth_rate (1/s) and jumping there when more than fight_snap_m (or half its speed in metres) off. A guest's hits on a copy land on the host's ship; a kill is everyone's, and the last wave down pays everyone in the fight. No word of the host's fight for fight_stale_s and it is over for the guest (fight_over says so). The host's fighters go for a guest in the fight as for the host: each guest's game sends where its ship is fight_rate times a second, and the host's hits on it land on that guest's ship. In town the host's guards and locals watch whichever player is nearest, a guest by the same standing as the host. Issue #402 (droids): the Remnant's and the locals' droids, the wreck's crew and the haulers go with the people (npc_rate, npc_far_m); a guest's copy closes on the host's at droid_smooth (1/s) and jumps when more than droid_snap_m off. Each player's own droids are sent to the others pal_rate times a second, and go from the others' games pal_timeout_s after the last word. The moon rave's laser droid is put back on the host's loop when more than rave_sync_s (seconds along it) off. One set of jobs (NetJobs): a job taken in any game (a drop, a bounty, a heist, the supply run, a board job) is everyone's, the host's game runs it; each game looks every jobs_every_s seconds whether its jobs changed and sends them (a guest's to the host, the host's to every guest). Pay, credits and gear stay each player's own.
